problem: City-scale outdoor navigation relies on dense maps or costly fine-grained supervision. Existing policies are trained on expert-only demonstrations and regress continuous waypoints, so they accumulate errors and cannot recover from deviations. Commercial-navigation directional instructions (e.g. 'turn right in 50 m') are too coarse for direct robot execution.
motivation: Commercial navigation tools (Google Maps, Amap) already provide mature global planning and real-time directional guidance, so using them could remove the need for dense maps and annotations. VLMs are better at reasoning on 2D images than regressing 3D waypoints. Long-horizon closed-loop navigation also needs explicit deviation assessment and recovery supervision.
key_idea: Reformulate direction-aware navigation as discrete spatial grounding on an egocentric image grid, with a CoT of deviation assessment, then corrective action, then grid trajectory, trained on a dataset with injected recovery trajectories (ReDA).
insight: Removing recovery data drops SR from 59.00 to 29.71 and CSR from 98.15 to 15.46, while DF stays low (1.31). Expert-only imitation is good in nominal states but cannot recover once OOD. Removing CoT drops SR to 38.91 and raises DF to 4.30 (18.75 in Town 15), showing structured reasoning stabilizes decisions. Note that the full model's DF (1.85) is higher than the w/o Recovery Data variant's (1.31).
method: Task formulation: input is the last 5 egocentric RGB frames (k=4) plus a discrete directional instruction from a commercial navigation tool (FORWARD/TURN_LEFT/TURN_RIGHT/STOP); output is a local trajectory of discretized image-plane grid cells.

Egocentric grid trajectory representation: a grid over rows 13-23 and cols 0-28 covers traversable regions; the future path is L=6 grid points (3 s at 2 Hz); the CoT output Y=(deviation Yes/No, action incl. CORRECT_LEFT/RIGHT, grid sequence).

ReDA data pipeline in CARLA: a Stable/Drifting/Recovering FSM injects steering perturbations, recovers once lateral error is ≥0.35 m using an adaptive look-ahead, and discards drifting frames; 3D waypoints are spline-smoothed and projected to the image grid; ~286k samples (158k expert, 128k recovery), 2102 trajectories, 126 scenes.
VLM policy: Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct with frozen visual encoder and adapter, LoRA on attention blocks, next-token loss on the structured CoT output; the prompt encodes the grid.
Image-to-body-frame grounding: grid points are projected to metric body-frame waypoints using depth plus intrinsics, with an IPM flat-ground fallback when depth is unreliable.

Furthest-point control: track only the last waypoint w_{t+L}; the heading-error controller gives saturated angular velocity and linear speed switches between v_nom and v_low depending on steering magnitude.
Real-world stack: robot streams RGB to a remote RTX 4090 server, and a parser converts smartphone navigation-app text into the instruction I_t.

setting.training_data: ReDA: ~286k samples (158k expert + 128k recovery frames), 2102 trajectories in 126 CARLA scenes (Towns 01-05, 10HD)
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB history (5 frames); depth optional at deployment for projection
setting.action_space: discrete image-plane grid targets (6-step) projected to body-frame waypoints, executed via furthest-point velocity control (v, ω)
setting.privileged: none at test time (directional instructions from commercial navigation tools; baselines get path priors)

numbers.eval_set_note: 239 long-horizon closed-loop trajectories across seen and unseen towns (Towns 06, 07, 15 unseen)
numbers.extra: trained on ReDA; baselines use official pretrained weights

numbers.eval_set_note: 2 scenarios (urban, park) x 5 paths >100 m x 3 repeats = 30 trials, Unitree Go2

numbers_note: The abstract claims 56.16% SR in unseen environments, but the per-town unseen results are only in a figure. The text states the SR drop from seen to unseen is 7.28%. The overall table gives 59.00.
results: In CARLA on 239 trajectories, DA-Nav reaches SR 59.00, SPL 58.66 and CSR 98.15, beating the strongest baseline ViNT (SR 51.88, CSR 23.54); SR is 56.16 on unseen towns. In the real world on a Go2 it achieves 46.7% SR versus 23.3% for CityWalker and 16.7% for ViNT, and transfers zero-shot to a humanoid for 1.2 km of navigation.
limitations: Depends on commercial navigation tools, so GPS error, latency and unmapped areas affect it.
Real-world closed-loop SR is still under 50%, and the real-world evaluation is small (30 trials) with only two baselines.
Remote VLM inference on a GPU server adds latency, and a flat-ground/depth-based projection is assumed.
